the extended delo-calization of electrons and the presence of intra-molecular hydrogen bond in the radicals are the two most important factors to determine the radical scavengig activities of phenolic acids.
the extended delocation and intra-molecular H bonds are the two major contributions to the stability and the radical scavengig activities of the phenolic acids and their derivatives.
the extended delocazation and intra-molecular H-bonds are the main contributions to the radical stability, which is the key to the radical scavengig activities.

the antioxidant activities of phenolic acids and their derivatives.
the antioxidant mechanisms of phenolic acids and their derivatives, and the underlying structure-activity relationships, which may be useful to the design of new antioxidants.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the extended conjugation, the intra-molecular hydrogen bond and the orthodiphenolate functionalities are the key factors to improve the radical scavengng activities of phenolic acids and their derivatives.

the presence of the extended conjugated system, the presence of the C = O or the C = C in the COOH, COOH, COOOR or the COOR groups, the orthodiphenol, and the absence of the single OH group at the ortho position are the key features that favorably contribute to the radical scavengng activities of these compounds.

the extended deloacalization of the phenolic ring, the presence of the ortho-diphenolic functionalities, and the intra-molecular hydrogen bonding are the main factors that contribute to the radical scavengng abilities of phenolic acids and their derivatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radical scavengenging activity of these phenolic compounds is determined by their structures and micro-environments.
the radical scavengaging activities of the phenolic acids and their derivatives are governed by the extended delocalized structures and intra-molecular H-bonds.
the radical scavengng activity of the natural phenolic acids is mainly governed by the stability of the corresponding radical species and the working mechanisms.

both the structure-thermochemistry-antioxidant activity relationships and the underlying working mechanisms of the phenolic acids and their derivatives can be well understood by using a combined theoretical-experimental approach.
